description: Machine-readable descriptor of the three EarthSciIO extensibility registries. Each registry is a name->implementation lookup. New backends register under a new name WITHOUT touching the Provider API. 'active' entries ship now; 'stub' entries are registered now (exercised via the registries by esio-9nb.8) and implemented later. The Provider depends only on the three interfaces named here.

transport.purpose: Fetch a resolved URL's bytes into the cache (conditional GET, auth, mirror failover). Bypassed entirely in offline mode.

entries.name: file
entries.notes: Expands ${EARTHSCIDATADIR} inside file:// templates; local copy into cache.

entries.name: cds
entries.notes: Copernicus CDS API v1: cds://<dataset>?<canonical-request-json> is submitted (POST .../execution), the job is polled to completion, and the result asset href is downloaded into the cache. Auth via the 'cds' realm (PRIVATE-TOKEN from ~/.cdsapirc or $CDSAPI_KEY).

entries.name: s3
entries.notes: Anonymous object GET: rewrites s3://<bucket>/<key> to regional virtual-hosted HTTPS (https://<bucket>.s3.<region>.amazonaws.com/<key>, region default us-east-2 via $EARTHSCI_S3_REGION/$AWS_REGION) and delegates to the http transport. No AWS SDK / SigV4; the s3:// URL stays canonical in the cache key + manifest.

format.purpose: Open a cached blob and return CF-decoded native-grid arrays keyed by file_variable. Does NOT remap variable names or apply unit_conversion (those stay in ESS).

entries.name: netcdf
entries.notes: CF decode: scale_factor/add_offset, _FillValue->NaN, time units/calendar retained raw. PROJECTION: the loader's `variables` are pushed into the decode (an unrequested variable is never decoded; coordinates are always returned; empty reads every variable; an absent name is an error listing what is present). TEXT VARIABLES ARE `string` FIELDS in every track, never skipped by any of them (an ERA5 `expver`, a `char label(n)`, a NetCDF-4 `NC_STRING`): a `char` variable's last dimension is the string length exactly when nothing else claims it as an axis (no coordinate variable of its own, and every variable using it is a `char` using it last), so `char label(n, strlen)` is n NUL-stripped strings and a 1-D `char label(strlen)` on a private dimension is a scalar string, while a `char label(n)` beside a `float value(n)` stays n one-character strings. Only a compound/opaque/enum/vlen variable has no array reading at all, and requesting one of those by name is an error naming its type. SELECTION: honours an orthogonal `select` at DECODE time -- one blob is still fetched under the same sha256(url) key, but only the requested hyperslab is materialised, so supports_selection is true while store_backed stays false. Axes are the shared 0-based vocabulary ("all" / {indices} / {slice}), positional over the file-order dims of the DECODED FIELDS whose rank matches, applied by dimension NAME to every array AND every coordinate -- text fields included, so a `char label(n)` loses the same cells its numeric neighbours lose. A consumed string-length dimension is NOT an axis and never enters that positional match (`char label(n, strlen)` is a RANK-1 field), so no selector can bind to it and a selection naming one is an error, not a silent no-op: slicing a string length would truncate every string rather than choose cells. A time axis that is not "all" is refused, because record selection is the Provider's (records_per_sample). RECORDS: `records` = {dim, indices} is the separate option through which that Provider pushes the records it chose -- absolute, file-local, 0-based, honoured in the order given, duplicates legal (the end-of-data bracket is [last, last]), an out-of-range index / an unknown dim / an empty list / a select narrowing the same dim all errors. `dim_length(reader, path, dim)` reads the header alone and is what makes those indices computable before the decode they narrow. Per-track availability of every decode option and metadata query is declared in `reader_options` / `metadata_queries` below, not in this prose: an out-of-process caller reads THAT to know what the binding it is talking to can actually do.

reader_options.name: variables
reader_options.purpose: Projection: the on-disk file_variable names to decode. Empty/absent reads every data variable; coordinates are always returned; a name absent from the blob is an error listing what is present.

reader_options.name: select
reader_options.purpose: Decode-time orthogonal window (§2.2). Positional over the file-order dims of the arrays whose rank matches, then applied by dimension NAME to every array and every coordinate. A time axis that is not "all" is REFUSED: choosing records is not the reader's.

reader_options.name: records
reader_options.purpose: Record pushdown: the records the cadence OWNER has already chosen, in the file's own numbering. Absolute, file-local, 0-based, honoured in the order given; duplicates legal (the end-of-data bracket is [last, last]); an out-of-range index, an unknown dim, an empty list, or a select narrowing the same dim are all errors rather than a wrapped or widened read. The reader is told the records and never the cadence.

extensions.julia: `indices` may also be a `len -> indices` CALLABLE, resolved against the axis length inside the reader's own open. An in-process convenience only -- the LIST is the wire form -- and it exists because the Julia Provider pushes down on every sample and would otherwise pay a second open per sample (measured 16.9 ms against the 2.9 ms the record selection saves on a GEOS-FP A1 file). Python and Rust reject a callable by name rather than accepting a spelling that cannot cross a process boundary.

reader_options.used_by_provider_note: Whether each track's Provider USES the option is a per-track performance decision, not a contract term: the option itself behaves identically in all three. The Julia Provider computes its record from the cadence and keeps no decoded-file buffer, so pushing down is a pure win. The Python and Rust Providers keep a decoded-file buffer (a 2-entry LRU) and amortise one whole-file decode over every tick in the file, so pushing down would REPLACE one decode per file with one per tick -- measured a 25.7x/3.0x per-tick regression in Python and 5.3x/2.3x in Rust on 24-record A1-shaped and 8-record A3dyn-shaped files. A `records` baked into a loader's reader_kwargs beside a cadence is REFUSED at construction in every track: it would narrow the record axis behind the Provider's own tick->record resolution, so every tick would read the same record and a 2-record bracket would degenerate to a constant field with no error anywhere.

metadata_queries.name: dim_length
metadata_queries.purpose: The length of one dimension, read from the blob's header and never from an array (§2.3). The whole-file counterpart of the store-backed array_shape, and what makes the `records` indices computable OUT OF PROCESS: they are a function of the file's length along the record axis, which has to be known before the decode they narrow. null when the reader cannot answer or the blob has no such dimension -- a caller must read that as "read whole and slice on my own side", never as an error.

entries.name: geotiff
entries.notes: Raster bands via GDAL; Python ships first, Julia/Rust may lag (R5). No binary fixture committed yet (no GDAL/git-lfs here).

entries.name: csv
entries.notes: Points readers: numeric columns->float64 1-D arrays, others->string.

entries.name: shapefile
entries.notes: ESRI shapefile as a feature table, decoded by a third-party library per track (pyshp / Shapefile.jl / the `shapefile` crate). ONE ROW PER PART: a record's parts (outer ring + holes, mainland + islands) each become one row of the `index` axis with the .dbf attributes replicated, plus shape_index/part_index/n_parts. `geometry` is float64[index, vertex, xy] right-padded to the longest part by REPEATING the final vertex (esm-spec 8.6.1), vertices stored verbatim (closing vertex kept, winding untouched). xmin/ymin/xmax/ymax are the record's STORED bbox replicated to its parts. shape_type and (when a .prj is present) crs_wkt are one-element `meta` string fields. dbf dtypes: N/F->float64 (blank->NaN), L->bool, D->YYYYMMDD string, C/M->string; `numeric_columns` forces named C columns to float64. `nvert_max` pads geometry to exactly that many vertex slots so the DOCUMENT declares the vertex-axis length (a longer part is an error naming the row, never a truncation). A row is deleted iff its dbf flag byte is `*` (0x2A) -- any other byte, NUL included, is live -- and a deleted row drops its shape too. A shapefile is a FILE SET but the cache holds one blob, so the fetchable form is a .zip: `member` names the .shp inside it (sidecars are the same stem), absent `member` requires exactly one .shp, and a bare .shp decodes geometry only. `member`/`numeric_columns`/`nvert_max` are reader config and never part of the cache key. Reader-only: no reprojection, no unit conversion, no ring-orientation fix, no hole classification, no name remap.

entries.name: ff10
entries.notes: FF10 point long-format (SMOKE/Emissions.jl FF10_POINT); '#' header skipped; fixed 77-col schema; numeric->float64 (blank->NaN), ids/codes/text->string; zip member via reader `member` kwarg; multi-member via `members` (explicit list) and/or `member_glob` (fnmatch-style */?/[...], case-sensitive) -- union, deduplicated, rows concatenated in ascending lexicographic (byte) member-name order; absent explicit member / zero-match glob is an error; directory placeholder entries (names ending `/`) are never selected; `member` mutually exclusive with `members`/`member_glob`; `skip_header_row` drops exactly one asserted `country_cd` header line per selected input (first non-comment line's first field must equal `country_cd` case-insensitively, else error -- never silently drops a data row). None of member/members/member_glob/skip_header_row are part of the cache key (the blob is the whole zip). Reader-only: no pivot/unit-convert/FIPS-SCC-normalize/EGU-filter.

entries.name: parquet
entries.notes: Apache Parquet as a FLAT TABLE: every column becomes a rank-1 native field over `index`, keyed by its on-disk column name; a table has no coordinates. Decoded by a third-party library per track (arrow-rs's `parquet` crate in Rust, pyarrow in Python, Parquet2.jl in Julia). Parquet carries an explicit logical type per column, so the dtype is a total function of the Arrow type rather than CF attribute sniffing: Boolean->bool; Int8/Int16/Int32/UInt8/UInt16->int32 and Int64/UInt32/UInt64->int64 (the SAME narrow/wide split as the netcdf reader); Float16/32/64 and Decimal128/256->float64 (unscaled value / 10^scale); Utf8/LargeUtf8/Utf8View->string; Dictionary(_,V) reads as V, expanded; Null->float64 all-NaN. A uint64 above int64::MAX is an error naming the row, never a wraparound. TEMPORAL COLUMNS RIDE AS THEIR RAW INTEGER, undecoded (Date32/Time32->int32; Date64/Time64/Timestamp/Duration->int64): the Arrow unit and timezone are NOT applied, the same rule a CF time axis gets, because turning an epoch offset into an instant is ESS's job. Nested and binary columns (list/struct/map/union/binary) have no rank-1 reading: naming one in `variables` is an error, and in read-everything mode it is simply not a native field. NULL POLICY: a null in a float column is NaN (the fold CF _FillValue gets) and fill_value stays null; a null in an integer, string or boolean column is an ERROR naming the column and row, because those types have no NaN and any default would be a real value silently standing in for a missing one. The reader options `null_int` (an integer sentinel, substituted AND reported back in fill_value like a surviving CF integer fill) and `null_string` open that gate only when a document declares them; a boolean has no such option (declare the column in `float_columns` if a third state is meant). `float_columns` forces named columns to float64 whatever their on-disk type -- the Parquet twin of shapefile's `numeric_columns` -- and does double duty: an integer column whose missing cells must be NaN, AND a column of fixed-decimal TEXT (corpora needing byte-reproducible floats store them as strings rather than IEEE doubles; the MOVES snapshots write meanBaseRate as "261.000000000000"). Text is trimmed and parsed; blank->NaN (the FF10/shapefile rule); anything else unparseable is an error naming the column, row and text. COLUMN PROJECTION IS PUSHED DOWN: the loader's `variables` become a Parquet ProjectionMask so only those column chunks are read off disk (these tables are wide and a document typically wants three columns); empty `variables` reads every column; a requested name absent from the file is an error listing what is present. A zero-row file is TYPED, not absent -- the schema lives in the footer, so every column comes back empty with its declared dtype. None of float_columns/null_int/null_string enters the cache key (they are decode-side). Reader-only: no row selection, no filtering, no code mapping, no name remap, no unit conversion -- esm-spec 8.9 puts codes/record_filter/select/extent downstream of the decode, and this reader honours no `select` (supports_selection is false, so the Provider hands it Selection::All unconditionally).

entries.name: zarr
entries.notes: Store-backed Zarr v2 reader: parses per-array .zarray/.zattrs (no consolidated .zmetadata), fetches ONLY the chunk objects a lazy orthogonal selection intersects (each chunk its own object, keyed by sha256(object_url)), blosc/lz4+shuffle decode, C-order unpack, <f4/<f8 -> float64, dims from _ARRAY_DIMENSIONS, no coordinate arrays. fill_value is NOT mapped to NaN.

store.purpose: Physical home of the content-addressed cache (blobs/meta/locks). Realizes the cache layout; the cache key (sha256(resolved_url)) is store-independent.

entries.name: local
entries.notes: $EARTHSCIDATADIR filesystem: blobs/<key[:2]>/<key>.<ext>, meta/<key>.json, locks/<key>.lock, tmp/<uuid>.part. flock advisory lock + atomic rename.

entries.name: s3
entries.notes: Object-store backend (key->object). Conditional PUT / If-None-Match as the lock analog. Registered as a stub.
